For current account holders, only one-way sales and withdrawals are permitted; after two years, all related websites, trading apps, and servers must be shut down. On the same day, the CSRC announced it would confiscate all illegal earnings of Tiger Brokers, Futu, and LongBridge and impose severe penalties. Official guidance stresses using legal channels such as the Hong Kong Stock Connect, QDII funds, and Cross‑Border Wealth Management Link for overseas investing. Meanwhile, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange explicitly states that personal foreign exchange may not be used for overseas real estate, securities investment, life insurance, or similar unapproved capital‑account purposes. Violators are placed on a “watch list,” lose their annual foreign‑exchange allowance for three years, face administrative penalties, possible anti‑money‑laundering investigations, and negative entries in their credit records (effective May 2026).
tips.sources: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2021). Personal Foreign Exchange Purchase Application Form (Attachment 1). <https://www.safe.gov.cn/safe/file/file/20210402/30fab7a9646f417ca9d2f67ff4c1e5f0.pdf>
tips.caveats: These regulations target foreign brokerage firms rather than individual investors; no penalties are specified for investors themselves. Those already holding accounts abroad need only sell and withdraw funds within two years. Each of the three legal channels has its own eligibility criteria — be sure to check with your bank or broker. Past strong performance of U.S. stocks does not guarantee future returns. When investing via QDII funds, follow the same principles outlined in items 17 (broad‑based index funds) and 19 (don’t concentrate assets in a single stock, platform, or market) — opt for diversified index funds rather than betting on one market. Separate limits apply to overseas cash withdrawals; see item 21.6 for details. This information is not investment advice.

tips.title: Insure only the losses your savings cannot absorb; use an emergency fund for the small ones
tips.cost: A premium is a real cost; compare the cover, the waiting period and the exclusions, not only the price. An emergency fund earns a modest interest.
tips.inPlainWords: Insurance is for a loss that would wreck your finances, not for every small expense. Buy health cover, term life cover if someone depends on your income, and motor third-party cover because the law requires it. Pay small repairs, a broken phone or a routine dental bill from an emergency fund. A policy with a low deductible and a high premium can cost more than the risk it covers.
tips.benefit: A health insurance policy and a term life policy transfer a catastrophic risk to the insurer. The IRDAI regulates the products and the claim process, and a policyholder has a grievance route. The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 requires at least third-party cover. An emergency fund of three to six months of expenses in a liquid account covers the small shocks and reduces the temptation to borrow.
tips.sources: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>; Policyholders' education. <https://policyholder.gov.in/>; Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, financial literacy. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>
tips.caveats: A policy excludes pre-existing conditions for a waiting period. A low premium can mean a high deductible or a narrow network. Do not cancel a health policy to save a small premium.

tips.title: If someone at home depends on your income, buy term life insurance for the breadwinner first — not for your kids.
tips.cost: A few hundred to a few hundred rupees per year, depending on age, coverage amount, and policy length (this is a rough estimate by the author; no official figures exist). Be sure to disclose your health status truthfully before applying; the process takes about half an hour.
tips.inPlainWords: Term life insurance covers you only for a set number of years. If you pass away during that period, your family receives a payout. This coverage is meant to protect dependents who rely on your earnings — for instance, if your mortgage is still unpaid or your children are still young. If no one depends on you financially, this insurance isn’t necessary. Since kids don’t earn income, laws also limit how much death benefit can be paid for them.
tips.benefit: Regulatory definitions classify life insurance as personal insurance where human lifespan serves as the insured event; it includes term life, whole life, and endowment policies. Term life insurance pays out only upon the insured’s death within a fixed timeframe. Whole life insurance remains valid for the entire lifetime. Accident insurance only compensates for death or disability caused by accidents; it doesn’t cover deaths from illness and thus cannot replace life insurance. Contracts requiring death payouts must be approved and agreed upon by the insured; otherwise they’re invalid. Parents may purchase death coverage for minor children without such consent, but total payouts for a child’s death cannot exceed statutory limits. Typical coverage amounts reach ₹14,21,000, and another ₹14,21,000 as well, hence the “high benefit” rating. No official recommendation exists for ideal coverage levels; the author’s calculation method adds remaining mortgage debt, projected expenses until children reach adulthood, and several years’ worth of household costs (based on national data revised in 2015).
tips.sources: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>; Policyholders' education. <https://policyholder.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: This C rating stems from the lack of official guidance beyond basic definitions and payout limits; the “prioritize adults” recommendation follows logically from “whoever loses income would jeopardize household stability.” A child’s death doesn’t reduce household income, whereas losing the primary earner leaves mortgage payments and child expenses unpaid. When funds are limited, prioritize term life and one-year medical coverage for adults before considering similar coverage for kids. For details on truthful disclosures and guaranteed renewability, see Section 7, Article 20 (one-year medical insurance). The designated beneficiaries here fall under Category ②: your spouse and children.

tips.title: Regretting a personal insurance policy signed for over a year? You can cancel it during the cooling-off period and get most of your premium back.
tips.cost: There’s no cost involved. A quick call to the insurer’s customer service line or a short visit to a branch takes just a few minutes. The real challenge is staying calm after signing and taking the time to read through the contract within 15 days.
tips.inPlainWords: All personal insurance policies with a term longer than one year include a cooling-off period. For policies bought through banks, this period starts 15 days after you receive the policy document, and cancelling during this time incurs a maximum administrative fee of ₹142. After this window closes, you’ll only receive the portion of your premium that the policy allows you to reclaim, which is usually far less than what you originally paid. Insurers often make follow-up calls to check if you fully understand the terms — be honest if you’re still unclear.
tips.benefit: Regulations require all personal insurance policies with a term over a year to clearly state the start date and length of the cooling-off period, as well as the rights policyholders have during this time. The cooling-off period for long-term health insurance must be at least 15 days. For all such policies sold via banks, the contract explicitly sets this period to 15 days, calculated from the natural calendar days after you receive and sign for the policy document. The policy cover must also carry this notice: “You have the right to cancel this policy in full (minus a maximum administrative fee of ₹142) within 15 days of receiving it. Cancelling after this period will result in financial losses.” Even after the cooling-off period ends, you can still terminate the contract at any time, and the insurer must refund the policy’s cash value — the portion of your premium that can be reclaimed — within 30 days as per contract terms. Financial regulators note that cancelling long-term personal insurance after the cooling-off period typically results in cash value payouts that are lower than the total premiums paid. Insurers must also reach out to new policyholders of such plans during the cooling-off period to confirm they’re aware of the potential financial losses from cancellation and their rights under this period (applicable nationwide since 2010 and 2019).
tips.sources: Ningxia Financial Supervision Bureau (2026-06-16). Risk tips on preventing illegal agency surrender. <https://www.nfra.gov.cn/branch/ningxia/view/pages/common/ItemDetail.html?docId=1261442&itemId=2188>; Reserve Bank of India. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Securities and Exchange Board of India. <https://www.sebi.gov.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The cooling-off period is a mandatory provision for all personal insurance policies with a term longer than one year. There’s no such requirement for one-year medical or accident insurance policies, so you’ll need to check the specific contract terms for these. For policies not bought via banks, the exact duration is defined in the contract — be sure to look up the “cooling-off period” clause as soon as you get the policy. Savings and dividend-paying insurance plans require higher premium payments, so making use of this period is especially worthwhile for these policies; see item 25 in this section for more details on non-savings plans. We rate the benefit as “moderate” because the savings you can achieve are the difference between your total premiums paid and the cash value you receive, which typically ranges from a few hundred to a few hundred rupees — no official statistics exist on this figure. You are the sole beneficiary of this provision.

tips.title: Before signing at the bank counter, check whether it’s a deposit or insurance
tips.cost: No cost at all. Just spend a couple of extra minutes reading the contract cover.
tips.inPlainWords: Banks may sell insurance on behalf of insurers, but they must not present it as a deposit. The contract cover must clearly state “Insurance Contract” and the insurer’s name in large print; terms like “deposit” or “savings” are strictly prohibited. If the insurer’s name appears on the cover, the money is not a deposit, and cancelling after the cooling-off period will result in losses. In principle, people aged 65 and older can only purchase insurance with guaranteed returns when buying at banks.
tips.benefit: Regulations explicitly forbid banks from bundling insurance with savings deposits, mutual funds, or other bank wealth products. They may not directly compare insurance returns to deposit yields, nor claim uncertain returns as guaranteed. Insurance documents and promotional materials must not use the bank’s name or logo, nor contain phrases such as “deposit,” “savings,” or “jointly offered by the bank.” The contract cover must display “Insurance Contract” in font size no smaller than 72 points and the insurer’s name in font size no smaller than 2 points. For three specific groups of customers, only insurance products with guaranteed benefits may be sold: applicants aged over 65; applicants aged over 60 purchasing installment-payment plans; and applicants whose annual income is below the local per capita disposable income. Policies for these groups must be manually underwritten by insurers rather than issued automatically at bank branches. Insurance agents are prohibited from selling insurance inside bank premises. For any insurance policy sold by a bank with a term longer than one year, a 15-day cooling-off period applies; cancelling after this period incurs financial losses. (Nationwide, effective October 2019)
tips.sources: Reserve Bank of India. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: This item is rated B because the regulations are very clear, yet no official statistics exist on how much money misled consumers have lost. Elderly family members are especially vulnerable to this issue when making deposits at banks; be sure to check the contract cover for them. If you’ve already signed such a contract, you may cancel it within 15 days per Section 42 (Cooling-off Period). For complaints regarding potential misrepresentation, refer to Section 44 (Assistance with Policy Cancellation). The primary beneficiaries of this guidance are you and your elderly relatives.

tips.title: To cancel your insurance policy, contact the insurer directly — don’t use “policy cancellation agents.” If you feel misled, call 12378 for free assistance.
tips.cost: There’s no cost involved. Simply call the insurer’s customer service line or visit a branch; this may require a bit more effort than using an intermediary.
tips.inPlainWords: Online ads promising “full policy refunds with no fees if unsuccessful” usually come from illegal cancellation agents. They typically take 30–50% of any refund amount and demand your ID, bank details, and verification codes. Once the policy is cancelled, coverage ends. If you feel misled, first contact the insurer’s customer service; if that fails, call 12378 — this service is completely free.
tips.benefit: It stated that claims of “full policy refunds” are false and contrary to insurance laws. “Policy cancellation agents” charge hefty fees; if you try to withdraw from their services, they may sue you for “breach of contract.” They also collect personal data such as SIM cards, bank accounts, policy details, home addresses, and even children’s school information — data that can be sold on, leading to fraud or identity theft. A June 2026 notice from Ningxia’s financial regulator provides further detail: such agents demand 30–50% of the refund amount as a fee and impose steep penalties if you back out. They even instruct clients to fabricate claims of sales misrepresentation or forged signatures. Following such advice could violate public security laws; in severe cases, it may constitute slander or extortion. Once cancelled, coverage ends immediately. Future applications for similar policies may be rejected or cost more due to age or health issues. If you truly feel misled, first contact the insurer’s official customer service; if unresolved, call 12378. If you’re temporarily unable to pay premiums, ask the insurer about options like reduced paid-up value or policy loans. Reduced paid-up value means you stop paying premiums, though coverage decreases proportionally (nationwide, 2026).
tips.sources: Ningxia Financial Supervision Bureau (2026-06-16). Risk tips on preventing illegal agency surrender. <https://www.nfra.gov.cn/branch/ningxia/view/pages/common/ItemDetail.html?docId=1261442&itemId=2188>; Hunan Financial Supervision Bureau (2025-07-23). Risk tips on preventing illegal "agency surrender" of black and gray products. <https://www.nfra.gov.cn/branch/hunan/view/pages/common/ItemDetail.html?docId=1218753&itemId=1480>
tips.caveats: In 2025, Hunan’s financial regulator reported a case: a woman followed “advice” from a “friend” to use a cancellation agent, paying a “consultation fee.” Ultimately, her policy was refunded only at its cash value. Three months later, she was diagnosed with breast cancer — and no longer had critical illness coverage. You must weigh the pros and cons: if coverage remains valuable, consider reduced paid-up value instead of cancellation. If you’re still within the cooling-off period, see Section 42 (Cooling-off Period). Your own well-being is the ultimate priority.

tips.title: Writing a specific beneficiary on the policy lets family claim the payout: 5 years for life insurance, 2 years for other policies
tips.cost: No cost involved. You fill this in once at purchase; any later changes to the beneficiary require written notice to the insurer.
tips.inPlainWords: If no beneficiary is listed, or if the named beneficiary passes away first, the payout is treated as part of the deceased’s estate and must first cover any debts owed by the deceased. If “Spouse: [Name]” is listed as beneficiary but the couple later divorces, the policy is effectively treated as having no beneficiary at the time of a claim. Family members must be aware of the policy’s existence: for life insurance, claims must be filed within 5 years of learning of the insured’s death; for other policies, the deadline is 2 years. In total, 100,000 people are affected by such situations, and another 100,000 face related complications.
tips.benefit: In three specific scenarios, payouts are classified as part of the insured’s estate and distributed per standard inheritance rules: 1) No beneficiary is named, or the designation is ambiguous; 2) The named beneficiary dies before the insured, with no other eligible beneficiaries; 3) The beneficiary legally loses or voluntarily waives their right to benefits, again with no other eligible beneficiaries. If both the insured and beneficiary die in the same incident with no clear order of death, the beneficiary is presumed to have died first. Any payout classified as an estate must first settle all outstanding taxes and debts owed by the deceased, with remaining funds distributed to heirs. Supreme Court rulings clarify that if a beneficiary is listed only by name and familial relationship, any subsequent change to that relationship renders the designation invalid. Unnotified changes to beneficiaries hold no legal weight with insurers. The statute of limitations for filing claims is 5 years for life insurance and 2 years for other policies, both starting from the date the claimant learns or should have learned of the insured’s death. Given that typical life insurance payouts reach hundreds of thousands of rupees, this benefit is rated as “high” (national data, revised 2015, effective 2021).
tips.sources: Insurance Act, 1938. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Once the statute of limitations expires, insurers may legally deny payouts, and legal action to recover funds is highly unlikely to succeed. For this reason, family members must at minimum know which insurers you hold policies with. After events like divorce, remarriage, or the birth of a child, update the beneficiary designation accordingly. To claim payouts after a death, follow the steps outlined in Section 25, Item 9 (claiming funds from multiple policies individually). Note that using the policy payout to settle the deceased’s debts is not a viable option; see Section 29, Item 13 (debt settlement) for further details. The beneficiary category for this item falls under Tier ②, which includes your spouse and children.

tips.title: Do not speculate in virtual currencies like Bitcoin or Tether, and do not follow others into crypto schemes: crypto transactions are not legally protected, and losses cannot be recovered in court
tips.cost: Zero financial outlay. Do not buy cryptocurrency tokens, and refuse invitations to join "signal-calling" or "guaranteed profit" crypto investment groups. The only trade-off is foregoing speculative gains during cryptocurrency bull runs.
tips.inPlainWords: Domestic legal frameworks do not recognize virtual currencies as legal tender. Private transactions exchanging fiat currency for cryptocurrency tokens can be judged legally null and void, meaning any resulting financial loss is borne entirely by the individual investor. In a documented case, an investor purchased approximately ₹63,66,100 ($63,000 USD) worth of Tether (USDT) through peer-to-peer sellers; when the exchange disabled withdrawals and shut down, his lawsuit seeking recovery was dismissed by the courts.
tips.benefit: The directive affirms that virtual currencies such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tether "lack legal tender status and must not and cannot circulate as currency in the market." Exchanging fiat currency for virtual currency, token-to-token trading, and initial coin offering (ICO) financing constitute illegal financial activities that are strictly prohibited, alongside overseas entities providing services to domestic residents. Regarding individual investments, the regulatory notice explicitly mandates: "Where any entity or individual invests in virtual currencies, real-world asset (RWA) tokens, or related financial products in violation of public order and good morals, the relevant civil legal acts are null and void, and any resulting losses shall be borne entirely by the parties themselves." In judicial practice, a plaintiff (Tang) purchased Tether (USDT) totaling ₹63,66,100 from platform merchants between 2018 and 2019. When the trading platform froze withdrawals and became unreachable, Tang filed a civil lawsuit to recover the funds. The court ruled that exchanging fiat currency for virtual currency was an invalid investment activity, held Tang personally responsible for all financial losses, and dismissed the lawsuit—a verdict upheld on appeal (Yixing People's Court, Jiangsu). Criminal theft of private keys or wallets is prosecuted differently: when hackers illicitly breached accounts to steal over 4 million rupees worth of crypto assets, the perpetrators were convicted of larceny and sentenced to 7 years' imprisonment alongside criminal fines.
tips.sources: Yixing People's Court (2025). Civil Judgment on Risk Assumption in Virtual Currency Investment Losses. <https://yx.wxfy.gov.cn/article/detail/2025/09/id/8970543.shtml>; Federal Bureau of Investigation (2022). Scammers Target and Exploit Owners of Cryptocurrencies in Liquidity Mining Scam (Alert Number I-072122-PSA). <https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2022/PSA220721>; Reserve Bank of India. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Securities and Exchange Board of India. <https://www.sebi.gov.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The principle of "losses borne entirely by oneself" governs civil disputes between token buyers, sellers, and trade leaders: civil courts will not enforce contracts or assist in recovering speculative investment principal, making post-loss litigation futile. If tokens are stolen or obtained through fraudulent cybercrime, file an immediate police report under criminal fraud/theft statutes. Existing token holders must also safeguard against malicious authorization phishing: in Jiangsu, a victim scanned an in-person QR code and inadvertently granted smart contract approval, resulting in 57,000 USDT (~₹55,98,700) being instantly drained from his wallet. The US FBI warned of similar liquidity mining scams where signing deceptive smart contract permissions allows attackers to drain wallet balances without further user consent. Protection: never connect Web3 wallets to unverified portals, and periodically audit and revoke token approvals using verified third-party allowance checkers. Allowing third parties to route illicit funds through your personal bank accounts to buy crypto constitutes criminal aid (see Chapter 9, Rule 5). Identifying high-yield financial traps is covered in Chapter 5, Rule 6; legitimate channels for overseas asset allocation are detailed in Chapter 5, Rule 38. This does not constitute investment advice. Benefit magnitude is categorized as High based on avoiding total loss of liquid capital. Primary beneficiary is yourself.

tips.title: Self-employed? Build a pension with NPS, PPF or EPF — there is no single 'minimum bracket' trick
tips.cost: The NPS charges a fund-management fee; the PPF has a low interest rate but no market risk. The contribution is the main cost.
tips.inPlainWords: A self-employed person has no employer pension. The main routes are the National Pension System, the Public Provident Fund and, for a covered establishment, the EPF. The NPS gives a tax deduction under section 80CCD(1B), the PPF is a safe long-term saving, and the EPF is available only through an eligible employer. Start early and contribute regularly; a last-minute contribution buys less pension.
tips.benefit: The NPS, the PPF and the EPF have different contribution, lock-in, return and tax rules. The PFRDA regulates the NPS, and the PPF is a government-backed small-saving scheme. A self-employed person can open an NPS tier-I account and choose the allocation; the PPF has a 15-year term that can be extended. The EPF requires an establishment covered by the EPF Act. The right mix depends on age, risk and liquidity.
tips.sources: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority. <https://www.pfrda.org.in/>; National Pension System. <https://www.npscra.nsdl.co.in/>; National Savings Institute, PPF. <https://www.nsiindia.gov.in/>; Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The tax rules and the contribution limits change. An NPS annuity is taxable in part. Do not put all your retirement money in one product. Check the PFRDA and the PPF rules.

tips.title: Inspect a new vehicle before delivery and keep the invoice, warranty and RTO papers
tips.cost: No cost to inspect. A professional PDI costs a small fee and can reveal a repaired vehicle.
tips.inPlainWords: Before you take delivery, inspect the paint, the tyres, the odometer, the lights and the spare wheel, and check that the VIN matches the invoice. Keep the invoice, the warranty booklet, the insurance and the registration papers. A defect in the first months is a warranty claim; a major defect can be a consumer complaint. Do not accept a vehicle with a repaired panel or a mismatched VIN.
tips.benefit: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 covers a manufacturing defect and a deficient service. The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the Central Motor Vehicles Rules require a valid registration and insurance. The warranty is a contract term, and a refusal to honour it can be a consumer complaint. A pre-delivery inspection (PDI) report signed by the dealer is evidence. The RTO registration and the VIN should match.
tips.sources: Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. <https://morth.nic.in/>; National Consumer Helpline. <https://consumerhelpline.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A 'zero kilometre' claim can be false; check the odometer and the manufacturing date. Do not sign the delivery note before the inspection. A used car needs a different check.

tips.title: When buying a used car from a dealership, check insurance claims and maintenance history, and specify in the contract that it is free of collision and flood damage; deliberate concealment entitles you to return the car with triple damages
tips.cost: A few dozen to hundreds of rupees for professional third-party vehicle inspection and VIN historical database queries. Spending 1 to 2 hours reviewing insurance loss claims and maintenance records prior to signing. Ensuring explicit condition representations are written into the purchase contract. Pursuing legal action if defrauded can require 1 to 2 years of proceedings.
tips.inPlainWords: When purchasing a used vehicle from a licensed commercial dealer who intentionally conceals past major collisions, structural frame damage, or water submersion, consumer protection laws allow you to rescind the sale, return the vehicle, and claim triple the purchase price in punitive damages. However, triple damages apply only if you prove the dealer knew and deliberately concealed the condition. If the dealer was genuinely unaware and the court agrees, remedies are limited to contract rescission, full refund, and statutory interest. Triple damages do not apply to private party sales between individuals.
tips.benefit: Under the Measures for the Administration of Used Car Circulation, commercial sellers are legally required to provide authentic disclosures regarding vehicle usage, maintenance history, accident records, roadworthiness inspections, security interests/liens, and statutory retirement dates. If seller fraud or concealment prevents vehicle title transfer, the seller must unconditionally refund the purchase price. Furthermore, Article 55 of the Consumer Rights Protection Law stipulates that where a commercial operator commits fraudulent misrepresentation in supplying goods, the consumer is entitled to punitive damages equal to three times the purchase price (minimum ₹7,100). In a landmark judicial precedent in Rizhao, Shandong, a consumer purchased a used vehicle for ₹7,53,100 with dealer assurances that it had never suffered a major collision. Subsequent professional appraisal revealed prior major crash damage, and historical insurance databases confirmed the car had previously been written off as a constructive total loss. The court rescinded the sales contract, ordered a full refund of ₹7,53,100, and awarded triple damages of ₹22,59,400, which was affirmed on appeal by the Rizhao Intermediate People's Court in 2025. Conversely, where evidence does not substantiate deliberate dealer knowledge—such as prior minor accident repairs occurring before the dealer acquired the car—courts may rule the dispute a breach of contract rather than statutory fraud, granting full rescission, refund, and interest without punitive triple damages (Zhengzhou Intermediate People's Court).
tips.sources: Shandong Legal Daily (2025). Used Car Dealership Conceals Accident History; Court Orders Contract Rescission and Triple Damages. <http://www.sdcourt.gov.cn/rzzy/404983/404968/41465920/index.html>
tips.caveats: Even if dealer contracts contain boilerplates like "vehicle sold in as-is condition," insist on adding explicit written guarantees that the vehicle has "no structural accident history, no water immersion, and no fire damage" to establish clear benchmark warranties. Because litigation can span multiple years, investing in independent pre-purchase mechanical inspections and checking official vehicle insurance claims registries before payment is far more cost-effective. New car lemon law protections are detailed in Chapter 5, Rule 47; calculating effective APR on auto financing is covered in Chapter 5, Rule 7. Benefit magnitude is categorized as High based on substantial financial recovery. Primary beneficiaries are yourself and your family.

tips.title: At a car dealership, refuse unauthorised 'financial service' fees and check every line of the invoice
tips.cost: No cost to ask. A loan from your bank may be cheaper than the dealer's offer.
tips.inPlainWords: A car dealer may charge for the vehicle, GST, registration, insurance and an optional accessory, but it cannot add an undisclosed 'financial service' fee or force you to buy insurance or a loan from it. Ask for a written break-up before you pay, and compare the loan terms with your bank. A forced add-on can be an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
tips.benefit: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 prohibits an unfair trade practice and a restrictive trade practice. The RBI's fair-practice rules apply to a loan, and the IRDAI rules apply to insurance; a lender or insurer cannot be forced on you. The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 requires the registration and the third-party insurance. A written quotation and the invoice are the evidence. A dealer cannot retain the registration certificate for an add-on.
tips.sources: Consumer Protection Act, 2019. <https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/>; Reserve Bank of India, fair practices. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>; Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. <https://irdai.gov.in/>; Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. <https://morth.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A genuine service fee should be disclosed and agreed. A 'discount' can hide a higher interest rate. Do not sign a blank delivery note or a loan form.

tips.title: If taken to designated shopping stores not specified in your group tour contract, demand a full refund through the travel agency within 30 days of trip completion, with the agency advancing the refund
tips.cost: Zero financial cost. During the trip, retain your signed travel contract, itinerary, sales invoices, and card payment receipts; keep purchased merchandise unboxed and unused. Upon return, contact the travel agency to arrange return shipping. If disputes arise, filing an official complaint and mediation may take 1 to 2 months.
tips.inPlainWords: Organizing low-cost tour groups to trap travelers into shopping, or taking travelers to commercial shopping stores not agreed upon in advance, violates tourism laws. Within 30 days after the tour ends, you have the legal right to require the travel agency to process returns and advance the refund money upfront. However, if you voluntarily signed a "voluntary shopping" supplementary agreement beforehand, that constitutes consent, making refunds much harder to obtain.
tips.benefit: (2) Travel agencies may not arrange specific shopping destinations unless mutually agreed upon through negotiation or explicitly requested by tourists without impacting other tour participants (signing a supplementary agreement generally constitutes mutual consent). (3) Where a travel agency violates either provision, the tourist has the statutory right within 30 days after the tour concludes to demand that the travel agency handle merchandise returns and advance the refunded money upfront; tourists may also demand full refunds for separate paid activities. This right does not require proving that the merchandise is defective or substandard. Article 9 further guarantees tourists the right to refuse compulsory transactions. In 2025, the Ministry of Culture and Tourism highlighted an enforcement case: a Chengdu travel agency organized a 15-tourist trip to Jiuzhaigou collecting only ₹85,500 total in tour fees, paid ₹1,16,800 to an intermediary to "buy the tour group," and extracted ₹1,94,800 in shopping kickbacks; the agency was fined ₹11,36,800 and suspended for 30 days. In 2024, the Guangdong Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism published a mediation case where two tourists on an ₹11,400 Hong Kong-Macau-Zhuhai package tour purchased over ₹2,84,200 of jewelry and latex bedding in duty-free stores; following a complaint to cultural tourism authorities, the travel agency mediated an agreement, coordinated return shipping, and advanced the full refund of all purchase funds.
tips.sources: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (2026). Measures for the Handling of Tourism Complaints (Ministry Order No. 14, Articles 11, 14, 23). <https://zwgk.mct.gov.cn/zfxxgkml/zcfg/bmgz/202602/t20260211_964700.html>; General Office of the Ministry of Culture and Tourism (2021). Circular on Optimizing Government Service Hotlines. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-11/19/content_5651873.htm>; Ministry of Culture and Tourism (2025). Typical Cases of Compulsory Consumption in the Tourism Market (Batch 3, Case 15). <https://www.mct.gov.cn/whzx/whyw/202509/t20250908_962084.htm>; Guangdong Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism (2024). Typical Tourism Complaint Cases of 2024 (Case 1). <https://whly.gd.gov.cn/service_newscgldt/content/post_4385141.html>
tips.caveats: Direct your refund claim to the domestic organizing travel agency, not the overseas or third-party merchant store. Complaints must be lodged within 90 days after contract performance completes, with mediation generally completed within 60 days of acceptance. If administrative mediation fails, civil litigation or arbitration is required; small-claims court procedures are covered in Chapter 8, Rule 22. If you signed a supplementary shopping consent form, refund arguments must rely on pricing discrepancies or misrepresentation. For overseas purchases, independent cross-border recovery is virtually impossible, making recourse against the licensed domestic agency essential. Senior citizens are frequently targeted with "zero-dollar tour" scams; elder financial fraud protections are detailed in Chapter 17, Rule 5. Primary beneficiaries are yourself and traveling family members.
